Access.description:
Whether an endpoint is read-only or mutates state.

Write endpoints are the ones an approval queue and the risk stage must gate (docs/archive/plan.md E11-S7), so the distinction has to be in the registry rather than inferred from the HTTP method.

oneOf.description: Mutates state; requires the risk stage and approval queue.

AccountConfig.description: Starting account state for a run.

oneOf.description: The exchange did not report an aggressor.

resume_from_seq.description: Replay the journal records with line index `>=` this value (0-based; default 0).

BacktestMetrics.description:
Headline performance numbers for a completed backtest.

A fixed, documented set rather than a free-form object, so a dashboard can bind to fields that are guaranteed present.

max_drawdown.description: Maximum peak-to-trough drawdown, as a positive fraction.

total_return.description: Total return as a fraction of initial capital.

BacktestRequest.description:
Backtest request.

Every field is optional on the wire, but `BacktestRequest::resolve` requires `seed` (non-zero), `strategy`, `universe`, `start` and `end` (ADR 0017 decision 6).

commission_per_fill.description: Flat commission charged on every fill, in the account's settlement currency; `None` or `0` charges none. Applied only by the `bar_fill` models (ADR 0017; see [`MAX_COMMISSION_PER_FILL`](crate::MAX_COMMISSION_PER_FILL)). Added in this request's first version, so an older client that omits it still parses.

fill_model.description: Fill model for this run, overriding the server's configured one: `bar_fill` (the default), `bar_fill_through`, `l2` or `none`. `l2` needs a tick source; without one the run fails with `l2_requires_ticks`. See [`FILL_MODELS`](crate::FILL_MODELS).

seed.description: Seed, for reproducibility; required and non-zero on submit. Same seed and data give a byte-identical journal.

slippage_bps.description: Slippage applied to every fill, in basis points of the fill price and always adverse to the order's side; `None` or `0` models none. Applied only by the `bar_fill` models. See [`MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS`](crate::MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS).

strategy.description: Strategy name or manifest id, as returned by `POST /strategies`.

assumptions.description: What the run did *not* model, stated explicitly.

error.description: Why the run failed; present only when `status` is `failed`.

BacktestRunConfig.description:
A complete, self-describing description of one backtest run.

This is the unit a caller submits. It names the strategy by manifest rather than by source, so the run cannot disagree with what was verified.

data.description: Where the market data comes from.

risk.description: Pre-trade risk limits (ADR 0018). Absent means no limits.

seed.description: Seed for every stochastic component. Same seed and data ⇒ identical journal.

Bar.description:
An aggregated OHLCV bar.

``` use honba_messages::{ Bar, BarAggregation, BarSpecification, BarType, InstrumentId, PriceType, UnixNanos, Exchange, };

let bar_type = BarType::new( InstrumentId::new("NIFTY50", Exchange::new("NSE")), BarSpecification::new(1, BarAggregation::Minute, PriceType::Last), ); let bar = Bar::new( bar_type, 22_000.0, 22_050.0, 21_980.0, 22_020.0, 15_000.0, UnixNanos::from_u64(1_700_000_060_000_000_000), UnixNanos::from_u64(1_700_000_060_000_000_000), ); assert_eq!(bar.open(), 22_000.0); assert_eq!(bar.close(), 22_020.0); ```

Invariants (checked by [`Bar::validate`] and on deserialization): all prices and the volume are finite, `low <= open, close <= high`, and `volume >= 0`.

BarAggregation.description: How a bar aggregates its underlying data.

BarSpecification.description:
Describes how a [`Bar`] aggregates its inputs.

``` use honba_messages::{BarAggregation, BarSpecification, PriceType};

let spec = BarSpecification::new(1, BarAggregation::Minute, PriceType::Last); assert_eq!(spec.step(), 1); assert_eq!(spec.aggregation(), BarAggregation::Minute); ```

`step` must be at least 1; deserializing a zero step fails.

BarType.description: Fully identifies a bar: which instrument, and how it aggregates.

BarsIngestRequest.description:
`POST /bars` request body: a batch of bars for the live bar pump (E3-S7 follow-up).

Each bar is validated on deserialization (finite prices, `low <= open, close <= high`, `volume >= 0`), so one bad bar rejects the whole batch. The batch size is bounded by [`crate::MAX_INGEST_BARS`]. Bars must ascend by `ts_event`; ordering is enforced downstream by the simulator, where an out-of-order bar is counted and skipped rather than failing the request.

bars.description: The bars to feed, oldest first.

BarsIngestResponse.description: `POST /bars` response: how many bars were handed to the bar pump.

accepted.description: Bars queued for the pump; the whole batch, or the request failed.

from.description: Inclusive start time, RFC3339 or ISO-8601 date.

to.description: Exclusive end time, RFC3339 or ISO-8601 date.

CapabilityManifest.description: Capability manifest describing what features are available.

endpoints.description: Endpoints in the contract, as `METHOD /path` in registry order.

not_implemented.description: The subset of `endpoints` that currently answer 501 `not_implemented`.

CompiledStrategy.description: A strategy that verified, with the id the server keeps it under.

id.description: Content id: `sha256:` plus the hex digest of the canonical manifest JSON. The same manifest always has the same id; a backtest names it as `strategy`.

ir.description: The verified IR the manifest compiled to.

passed.description: Whether alpha remains positive under $2\times$ cost stress.

retention_2x.description: Ratio of $2\times$ Sharpe to baseline Sharpe ($\text{Sharpe}_{2\times} / \text{Sharpe}_{1\times}$).

stress_3x_sharpe.description: Severe stressed ($3\times$ cost) annualized Sharpe ratio.

DataSourceConfig.description: Where a run reads market data from.

oneOf.description: Parquet files under a local root, read through `honba-feed`.
A broker adapter, resolved by name at run time.

DepthLevel.description: One side of the order book.

DsrResult.description: Result of Deflated Sharpe Ratio validation.

expected_max_sharpe.description: Expected maximum Sharpe ratio under the null hypothesis ($SR_0$).

passed.description: Whether DSR exceeds the required significance threshold.

standard_error.description: Standard error of the observed Sharpe ratio accounting for skewness & kurtosis.

ErrorCategory.description:
The broad area a failure came from.

Clients switch on this to decide *where* to react; the finer-grained [`ErrorCode`] says *what* happened. Splitting the two keeps client logic from depending on the full code list.

oneOf.description: The request was malformed or failed validation.
The caller exceeded a rate limit.
A pre-trade risk rule refused the operation.
The order lifecycle itself failed (rejection, unknown order).
Market data is missing, stale, or unavailable.
A timeout or transport-level failure; safe to retry.
The server failed for a reason it did not anticipate.
The operation is not supported on this surface or build.

ErrorCode.description:
One code per failure mode, stable across releases (docs/archive/plan.md §4.2).

Deserialization is deliberately strict: an unrecognized code is an error rather than a default, because silently mapping a newer server's code onto a known one would report the wrong thing happened.

``` use honba_messages::ErrorCode;

let code = ErrorCode::RiskMaxNotionalExceeded; assert_eq!(code.category().as_str(), "risk"); assert!(!code.is_retryable(), "a risk refusal is not worth repeating"); assert_eq!( serde_json::to_string(&code).unwrap(), "\"risk_max_notional_exceeded\"" ); ```

oneOf.description: A request was malformed or failed validation.
A named resource does not exist.
The caller is authenticated but not permitted to do this.
The caller exceeded a rate limit.
Order notional exceeded the configured maximum.
Position size exceeded the configured maximum.
Account drawdown exceeded the configured maximum.
The submitter refused an order because trading is halted (ADR 0018).
Orders per window exceeded the configured rate limit (ADR 0018).
Order quantity is below the instrument minimum (ADR 0018).
Order quantity exceeds the instrument freeze quantity (ADR 0018).
Order quantity is not a multiple of the lot size (ADR 0018).
Order price is non-positive or off the tick grid (ADR 0018).
Order price is outside the instrument price band (ADR 0018).
Order would not reduce the position while reduce-only (ADR 0018).
No trading rules exist for the order's instrument (ADR 0018).
Order quantity exceeds the configured participation fraction of ADV (ADR 0018).
Feed quote or bar data is stale relative to event time (E2-S10).
A market order's expected execution price is outside the price collar (ADR 0018).
The exchange or gateway rejected the order.
No execution engine is attached to receive the order (ADR 0018).
The referenced order does not exist.
The referenced instrument does not exist.
Market data is unavailable for the request.
The operation is not supported on this surface or build.
The route exists in the contract but its behaviour is not built yet.

ErrorDetail.description:
A single error as it crosses a surface.

Carries the stable [`ErrorCode`] plus human-readable detail. `context` holds structured specifics (the limit that was exceeded, the id that was not found) so a client can react programmatically without parsing `message`.

context.description: Structured detail specific to this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description. Never parsed by clients.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the identical operation is safe.

Event.description:
Any typed event that can flow through the Honba event kernel.

Serialized as an internally tagged JSON object: `{"type": "order_filled", ...}`.

``` use honba_messages::Event;

fn is_market_data(ev: &Event) -> bool { matches!(ev, Event::Quote(_) | Event::Trade(_) | Event::Bar(_)) } ```

oneOf.description: A new order that has been submitted.

avg_fill_price.description: Volume-weighted average fill price; `None` until a fill. Additive.

cancel_requested.description: A cancel was asked for and not yet answered (ADR 0019); only valid while the order is working.

filled_at.description: Event time of the latest fill the row has seen; `None` until a fill. Additive: lets a reader order fills across rows by fill time rather than by row order.

filled_qty.description: Cumulative filled quantity (`0` until a fill; omitted from the wire while `0`). Additive field: a reader without it decodes as `0` (ADR 0012 rule 1).

product.description: Broker product the order is placed under (ADR 0010); `None` when the venue does not distinguish. Additive field: a reader without it decodes as `None` (ADR 0012 rule 1).

reject_reason.description: Why the order (or its unfilled remainder) was refused; `None` otherwise. Additive.

trigger_price.description: Stop trigger price; `None` unless the order is a stop order.

ts_event.description: The exchange timestamp at which acceptance occurred.

venue_order_id.description: The venue's own id for the order, when the acknowledgement names one.

ts_event.description: The exchange timestamp at which rejection occurred.

oneOf.description: An order received a fill that left a remainder (ADR 0019).

cum_qty.description: The cumulative filled quantity after this fill (finite, `> 0`).

last_px.description: The price at which this fill occurred (finite).

last_qty.description: The quantity filled in this event (finite, `> 0`).

ts_event.description: The exchange timestamp at which the fill occurred.

oneOf.description: An order received the fill that completed it (since schema version 4; earlier fills are [`Event::OrderPartiallyFilled`]).

last_px.description: The price at which this fill occurred (finite).

last_qty.description: The quantity filled in this event (finite, `> 0`).

ts_event.description: The exchange timestamp at which the fill occurred.

oneOf.description: A cancel was asked for and not yet answered (ADR 0019).

ts_event.description: The timestamp at which the cancel was processed.
The exchange timestamp at which cancellation occurred.
The exchange timestamp at which expiry occurred.

apply_market_calendar.description: Whether the run applies the India trading calendar and holidays.

cost_model_version.description: Commission model version, recorded in the run's assumptions.

slippage_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to modelled slippage, for cost-stress reruns.

FillModel.description:
The fill model a run uses.

Named rather than free-form so a result can state exactly how it was filled; an unrecognised model would make results incomparable.

oneOf.description: Fill at the bar's open, next open, or a fraction of the bar's range.
Fill only when the bar trades through the order price.
Top-of-book matching against quote/trade ticks (ADR 0030). The run needs a tick source; a run whose data source supplies bars only is refused with `l2_requires_ticks`.
No fills; used to test the strategy's signal path alone.

FilterOp.description: Comparison operators for screener filter expressions.

oneOf.description: Crosses above threshold or second series
Crosses below threshold or second series

HttpMethod.description: The HTTP methods the API exposes.

InstrumentId.description: A trading instrument, combining a symbol and its exchange.

instruments.description: Matching instruments, as of the requested snapshot.

IrSubscriptions.description: Subscriptions after resolution: one sorted instrument list per channel.

bars.description: Instruments whose bars (on the driving timeframe) are delivered.

quotes.description: Instruments whose top-of-book quotes are delivered.

trades.description: Instruments whose trade prints are delivered.

instruments.description: The instruments it resolved to, sorted and de-duplicated.

named.description: The universe's name when the manifest named one (e.g. `NIFTY50`).

LayoutDocument.description: A workbench layout: any JSON value, opaque to the server.

LayoutsResponse.description: `GET /profile/layouts` response: the named layouts by name.

layouts.description: Layouts by name (opaque to the server).

Message.description:
The envelope that carries an [`Event`] plus Honba-side metadata.

This is the versioned unit of the wire contract: its JSON form is `{"schema_version": 4, "event": {...}, "ts_init": {...}}`, and deserializing a message with any other `schema_version` fails. Unknown fields, in the envelope or the event, are ignored (ADR 0012 rule 1): a newer producer's additive fields never break this reader, while a reshaped wire bumps the version and is rejected.

``` use honba_messages::{Event, Message, UnixNanos, QuoteTick, InstrumentId, Exchange};

let quote = QuoteTick::new( InstrumentId::new("NIFTY50", Exchange::new("NSE")), 22_000.0, 22_001.0, 50.0, 75.0, UnixNanos::from_u64(1), UnixNanos::from_u64(1), ); let msg = Message::new(Event::Quote(quote), UnixNanos::from_u64(2)); assert!(msg.event().is_market_data()); assert_eq!(msg.schema_version(), honba_messages::SCHEMA_VERSION); ```

schema_version.description: Rendered as a plain `u32` in the schema, matching the JSON wire form (the internal `SchemaVersion` unit type would otherwise emit `{}`).

MetricDefinition.description: Catalog definition of a metric (mirrors Python MetricDefinition).

filterable.description: Whether this metric can be filtered upon in scans.

hasPeriod.description: Whether this metric supports evaluation period dimension.

hasTimeframe.description: Whether this metric supports timeframe dimension.

key.description: Unique metric key sent to the backend.

sortable.description: Whether this metric can be sorted upon in scans.

valueType.description: Data type of the metric value.

MetricKeySpec.description: Specification of a requested metric with its evaluation dimensions.

MetricPeriod.description: Evaluation period dimension for fundamental or snapshot metrics.

MetricRef.description:
A metric used as the right-hand operand of a predicate.

Makes metric-to-metric comparisons expressible on the wire, e.g. `SMA50 crosses_above {"key": "SMA200"}`. `key` is the wire key, never a UI id.

key.description: Wire key of the referenced metric (e.g. `SMA200`).

MetricValue.description: Dynamic value of a metric in a screener row or symbol fact table.

Money.description: Monetary amount in integer minor units (see Currency minor_exponent).

MonteCarloResult.description: Results from block-bootstrap Monte Carlo analysis.

median_max_drawdown.description: Median maximum peak-to-trough drawdown across all simulated paths.

passed.description: Whether the strategy passed the Monte Carlo stability gate.

prob_loss.description: Probability of ending with negative return (loss probability).

prob_ruin.description: Probability of hitting or exceeding the ruin drawdown threshold.

Order.description:
A client order.

``` use honba_messages::{ InstrumentId, Order, OrderId, OrderSide, OrderStatus, OrderType, TimeInForce, UnixNanos, Exchange, };

let order = Order::new( OrderId::new("O-1"), InstrumentId::new("NIFTY50", Exchange::new("NSE")), OrderSide::Buy, OrderType::Limit, 75.0, Some(22_000.0), TimeInForce::Day, UnixNanos::from_u64(1), UnixNanos::from_u64(1), ); assert_eq!(order.status(), OrderStatus::Initialized); assert_eq!(order.quantity(), 75.0); ```

Invariants (checked by [`Order::validate`] and on deserialization): `quantity` is finite and `> 0`; `price` and `trigger_price` are finite when present; `cancel_requested` is `true` only while the order is `Submitted`, `Accepted` or `PartiallyFilled`. An order is a record (it may come back from an exchange), so `side` may be `no_order_side`; intents are stricter.

avg_fill_price.description: Volume-weighted average fill price; `None` until a fill. Additive.

cancel_requested.description: A cancel was asked for and not yet answered (ADR 0019); only valid while the order is working.

filled_at.description: Event time of the latest fill the row has seen; `None` until a fill. Additive: lets a reader order fills across rows by fill time rather than by row order.

filled_qty.description: Cumulative filled quantity (`0` until a fill; omitted from the wire while `0`). Additive field: a reader without it decodes as `0` (ADR 0012 rule 1).

product.description: Broker product the order is placed under (ADR 0010); `None` when the venue does not distinguish. Additive field: a reader without it decodes as `None` (ADR 0012 rule 1).

reject_reason.description: Why the order (or its unfilled remainder) was refused; `None` otherwise. Additive.

trigger_price.description: Stop trigger price; `None` unless the order is a stop order.

OrderIntent.description:
A strategy's desire to trade, before it becomes a concrete [`Order`].

Strategies emit intents; the runner converts them into orders with unique ids and timestamps. This indirection keeps strategies free of bookkeeping they shouldn't care about.

Price fields by order type (checked by [`OrderIntent::validate`], on deserialization, and by [`OrderIntent::into_order`], so an invalid intent built with a constructor or struct literal never becomes an [`Order`]):

| `order_type`    | `price` (limit) | `trigger_price` (stop) | `trail_*` (trailing stop) | |-----------------|-----------------|------------------------|---------------------------| | `Market`        | none            | none                   | none                      | | `Limit`         | required        | none                   | none                      | | `StopMarket`    | none            | required               | none                      | | `StopLimit`     | required        | required               | none                      | | `TrailingStop`  | none            | none                   | exactly one required      |

``` use honba_strategy::OrderIntent; use honba_messages::{InstrumentId, OrderSide, OrderType, Exchange};

let intent = OrderIntent::market_buy( InstrumentId::new("NIFTY50", Exchange::new("NSE")), 75.0, ); assert_eq!(intent.side, OrderSide::Buy); assert_eq!(intent.order_type, OrderType::Market); ```

time_in_force.description: How long the order remains active.

trigger_price.description: Stop trigger price, for `StopMarket` and `StopLimit` orders.

OrderRateLimit.description: At most `max_orders` approved orders in any `window_ms` of event time.

max_orders.description: Maximum approved orders per window; must be `>= 1`.

window_ms.description: Window length in milliseconds of event time; must be `>= 1`.

OrderSide.description: Which side of the book an order sits on.

OrderStatus.description: The current lifecycle state of an order.

oneOf.description: Sent to the exchange, awaiting acknowledgement.
Cancelled by the client or exchange.
Execute at the best available price.
Execute at or better than a limit price.
Become a market order when a stop price is touched.
Become a limit order when a stop price is touched.
Trailing stop: market order once triggered.

client_order_id.description: Client order id: the idempotency key (ADR 0019 decision 3). The ledger records the order under it; a repeat of the same key is a duplicate no-op that returns the first row.

tif.description: Time in force: day, gtc, ioc, fok.

ParamLocation.description: Which side of the transport a request body comes from.

ParameterSpec.description: A parameter declaration with a default value and optional sweep range (E4-S2).

default.description: Default value for the parameter.

PboResult.description: Result of Probability of Backtest Overfitting analysis.

combinations_evaluated.description: Number of symmetric cross-validation combinations evaluated.

median_oos_percentile.description: Median relative rank of the best In-Sample model out-of-sample ($\in [0.0, 1.0]$).

passed.description: Whether PBO is below the acceptable threshold.

PortfolioAccount.description: One account of a portfolio: cash, equity, margins and the positions it holds (ADR 0032 §2).

broker.description: The broker this account is synced from, when `source` is [`PortfolioSource::Broker`].

currency.description: The settlement currency of the account's amounts.

equity.description: Cash plus mark-to-market value of the open positions (and holdings).

greeks.description: Net aggregate option Greeks across positions, when options are present (OpenAlgo design).

id.description: Stable account id within the portfolio.

market_value.description: Mark-to-market value of the open positions (and holdings).

realized_pnl.description: Realized PnL summed over the account's positions.

source.description: Where the positions and funds come from (ADR 0032 §6).

unrealized_pnl.description: Unrealized PnL summed over the account's positions.

PortfolioAccountsResponse.description: `GET /portfolio/accounts` response: the valued accounts of the caller's portfolio (ADR 0032 §6). The full snapshot is `GET /portfolio`.

PortfolioGreeks.description: Net aggregate option Greeks across open positions in an account or portfolio (OpenAlgo design).

delta.description: Delta: sensitivity of position value to underlying price changes.

gamma.description: Gamma: sensitivity of Delta to underlying price changes.

vega.description: Vega: sensitivity to a 1% change in implied volatility.

PortfolioHolding.description: A delivery holding: a carried position, without an intraday side (ADR 0032 §2).

group_name.description: Logical group or sub-basket (from QuantDinger design: e.g. "Core", "Growth").

mark.description: The last mark used to value the holding.

realized_pnl.description: Realized PnL accrued on fills, in the account's currency.

tags.description: User or strategy tags (from QuantDinger design: e.g. ["largecap", "esg"]).

unrealized_pnl.description: Mark-to-market PnL, in the account's currency.

PortfolioHoldingsResponse.description: `GET /portfolio/holdings` response: the valued delivery holdings across the caller's accounts (ADR 0032 §6).

holdings.description: The valued delivery holdings, flattened across accounts.

PortfolioMode.description:
Whether an account holds real or simulated money (ADR 0032 §4).

Sandbox money must never mix with live money: totals are per mode and an order names its account. `Sandbox` is the default while no live venue exists.

oneOf.description: Real money, sourced from a live broker.
Simulated money (paper trading, backtest or the simulator).

PortfolioPosition.description:
A valued position held for a user (ADR 0032 §2).

`quantity` and the prices are observations (`f64`); the amounts are `Money` in the account's currency. `realized_pnl` is the ledger entry accrued per fill (ADR 0011); `unrealized_pnl` is `(mark - avg_price) * sign * quantity`, computed against the last mark.

group_name.description: Logical group or sub-basket (from QuantDinger design: e.g. "Core", "Hedge").

mark.description: The last mark used to value the position.

product.description: The product the position is held under (intraday/delivery/carry).

realized_pnl.description: Realized PnL accrued on fills, in the account's currency.

side.description: Long or short. The sign of `quantity` is carried here, not in the number.

strategy_id.description: Strategy tag attributing this position to an automated strategy (from OpenAlgo design).

tags.description: User or strategy tags (from QuantDinger design: e.g. ["tech", "dividend"]).

unrealized_pnl.description: Mark-to-market PnL, in the account's currency.

PortfolioPositionsResponse.description: `GET /portfolio/positions` response: the valued open positions across the caller's accounts (ADR 0032 §6). Delivery holdings are `GET /portfolio/holdings`.

positions.description: The valued open positions, flattened across accounts.

PortfolioSnapshot.description:
A valued, per-user portfolio: the response body of `GET /portfolio` (ADR 0032 §2).

`owner` is the request's `Caller` (`token_id` when auth is on, else `default`): one snapshot belongs to one user. `as_of` is stamped by the caller, never read from a clock here.

accounts.description: The accounts, in a stable order.

as_of.description: The time the marks were taken (`UnixNanos`).

base_currency.description: The base currency of the totals.

owner.description: The user this portfolio belongs to (`token_id` or `default`).

revision.description: Monotonic revision of the stored portfolio, bumped on every write.

PortfolioSource.description:
Where an account's positions and funds come from (ADR 0032 §2, §6).

An `Ledger` account is honba's own book: positions accrue from the execution path and the simulator. A `Broker` account is synced: positions and funds are read from a broker adapter and name the broker. Both project into the same [`PortfolioAccount`], so one contract serves both.

oneOf.description: honba's own ledger (fills and the simulator).
A broker account, read from an adapter.

PortfolioTotals.description: Totals across every account of a portfolio (ADR 0032 §2).

PriceType.description: Which price of the underlying data feeds the bar.

Product.description:
The holding period a broker applies to a position (ADR 0010).

This is the market-neutral vocabulary, not a broker's product codes: Zerodha's `CNC`/`MIS`/`NRML` and Dhan's `CNC`/`INTRADAY`/`MARGIN` live in the declarative mapping tables (`crate::orders::mapping`), never in the core enum.

oneOf.description: Held overnight and settled into the demat account.
Squared off before the end of the trading day.
Carried forward under a margin/derivatives product.

alerts.description: Alert rules (opaque to the server; may hold webhook URLs, visible only to this user).

layouts.description: Named workbench layouts (opaque to the server).

preferences.description: Preferences and theme (opaque to the server).

workbench.description: Workbench grid and the symbol in each pane (opaque to the server).

revision.description: The profile's revision after the write.

QuoteTick.description:
A top-of-book quote update.

``` use honba_messages::{InstrumentId, QuoteTick, UnixNanos, Exchange};

let tick = QuoteTick::new( InstrumentId::new("NIFTY50", Exchange::new("NSE")), 22_000.0, 22_001.0, 50.0, 75.0, UnixNanos::from_u64(1), UnixNanos::from_u64(1), ); assert_eq!(tick.bid_price(), 22_000.0); assert_eq!(tick.ask_price(), 22_001.0); ```

Invariants (checked by [`QuoteTick::validate`] and on deserialization): prices and sizes are finite, `bid_price <= ask_price`, sizes are `>= 0`.

as_of.description: Return the latest quote known at this time (RFC3339 or ISO-8601 date, inclusive); the latest held when omitted.

Reason.description: One detector firing, shown to the user verbatim (ADR 0031 §1).

code.description: Stable code from the frozen ontology (ADR 0031 §4), e.g. `ema_cross_up`.

label.description: Short human text, e.g. `20-EMA crosses above 50-EMA`.

weight.description: The positive term this detector contributed to the signal's `strength`.

ReasonGroup.description: The detector family a reason belongs to.

oneOf.description: Relative strength versus an index or peer.

ReasonPolarity.description: The direction a single reason argues for.

ResponseEnvelope.description:
A response body, always carrying both version axes and at most one of `data` / `error`.

Unknown fields are accepted on read so a v1 reader can consume a response from a newer writer that added an optional field; unknown *versions* are rejected by the caller, which compares `api_version` and `schema_version` against what it was built for.

api_version.description: Semantic version of the API surface.

data.description: Payload on success; absent on failure.

error.description: Error detail on failure; absent on success.

schema_version.description: Integer version of the wire shape (see [`SCHEMA_VERSION`](crate::SCHEMA_VERSION)).

RiskLimits.description: Per-run risk limits. `None` means the rule is off; the default has no limits.

max_notional.description: Per-order notional ceiling in major units of the account currency. `None` = no notional rule; `Some` must be finite and `> 0`.

max_participation.description: Maximum order quantity as a fraction of ADV. `None` = no participation rule; `Some` must be in `(0, 1]`.

order_rate.description: Orders-per-window ceiling in event time. `None` = no rate rule.

price_collar_bps.description: Market-order price collar in basis points (ADR 0018 addendum): a market order (and the market leg of a stop) is refused when its expected execution price deviates from the reference price by more than this. `None` = no collar; `Some` must be `>= 1`.

stale_after_ms.description: Maximum quote/feed age in milliseconds before an order is refused. `None` = no feed staleness rule; `Some` must be `>= 1`.

RunStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an asynchronous job.

`pending -> running -> completed | failed | cancelled`, plus `pending -> cancelled`. The three terminal states are final (ADR 0017 decision 1; the transition table is `RunStatus::next`). `Cancelled` was added within `/api/v1` (ADR 0012 rule 2); exhaustive decoders must be regenerated (rule 3).

oneOf.description: Finished with a failure; see `error` on the response.
Stopped before completing (ADR 0017: reachable only through graceful shutdown in v1).

ScreenerFilterGroup.description: Logical grouping of filter predicates (AND / OR).

ScreenerFilterPredicate.description:
Individual filter predicate applied to a metric key.

Deserialization enforces the value contract of [`check_predicate_value`].

key.description: Target metric key to filter by.

value.description: Target value, array of values, or a [`MetricRef`] object.

ScreenerQuery.description:
`GET /screener/scan` query parameters.

The structured values are JSON text inside the query string, so the whole request is one flat string map on every transport.

as_of.description: Evaluate on the bars known at this time (RFC3339 or ISO-8601 date, inclusive); the latest held when omitted.

filters.description: JSON-encoded filter group, `{"operator": "AND"|"OR", "items": [...]}`; items are predicates (`{"key", "op", "value"}`) or nested groups. Omitted means no filter: every instrument of the universe matches.

universe.description: JSON-encoded array of instrument ids (`["TCS.NSE", ...]`) to scan; required, at most `MAX_SCREENER_UNIVERSE` entries.

ScreenerResultRow.description: One instrument that passed a screener scan.

metrics.description: Latest value of every metric the filter reads, by key as written in the filter; `null` while a metric is still warming up.

ScreenerRow.description: Single scanned instrument row returned in screener responses.

values.description: Metric values keyed by metric spec string.

ScreenerScanRequest.description: Request payload for POST /api/v1/screener/scan (mirrors Python ScreenerScanRequest).

primaryOnly.description: Whether to only scan primary listings.

types.description: Instrument asset types to scan (defaults to ["EQUITY"]).

Signal.description:
An explainable buy/sell point at one closed bar (ADR 0031 §1).

`reasons` is never empty: a signal with no reason is a bug, not a weaker signal. Construct through the engine, or call [`Signal::validate`] after building one by hand.

anchor_price.description: The bar close, or the trigger level for a level break.

evidence.description: Numbers the reason text cites, for inspection. Omitted when empty.

horizon.description: The horizon ruleset that produced the signal.

instrument.description: The instrument the signal belongs to.

reasons.description: The reasons that fired at this bar; never empty.

strength.description: Confluence strength in `0..=1`: the winning side's share of fired weight.

t.description: Close time of the confirming bar.

timeframe.description: The bar timeframe the signal was evaluated on (e.g. `5m`, `1d`).

SignalHorizon.description: The trading horizon a signal was evaluated for (ADR 0031 §5).

oneOf.description: Intraday: session VWAP, opening range, no overnight.

SignalScanRequest.description: Request payload for the signal scan / `GET /signals` (ADR 0031 §6).

detectors.description: Restrict to these detector codes; empty means every detector in the ruleset.

minStrength.description: Drop signals weaker than this (`0..=1`); defaults to `0.0`.

SignalScanResponse.description: Response to a signal scan: the fired signals across the universe, newest last.

signals.description: The signals, ordered by `t` then instrument.

SortSpec.description: Sort direction and dimension for screener results.

Source.description: A source feeding a [`Module`], for example a broker adapter or a symbol list.

reference.description: Kind-specific reference (an adapter name, a list name, a directory).

StrategiesRequest.description:
`POST /strategies` request: the manifest to verify, compile and keep.

Source code is not accepted (`code` or `source` is a 422 with `reason = source_unsupported`); a manifest is the only input a server can verify without running author code.

manifest.description: The strategy manifest, as accepted by `POST /strategies/verify`.

StrategiesResponse.description: Strategies response: the compiled strategies of this process, ordered by id.

StrategyIr.description: A verified strategy, ready to run: the manifest plus everything resolved from it.

driving_timeframe.description: The bar timeframe that drives the strategy's clock.

schema_version.description: Wire version of this document; readers reject any other value.

strategy_api_version.description: Strategy contract version the manifest was compiled against.

subscriptions.description: What is fed to the strategy, per channel.

timeframes.description: Every bar timeframe the run must load, driving timeframe first.

universe.description: The concrete instrument set the strategy may trade.

warmup_bars.description: Driving bars consumed before the first decision (the manifest's `warmup_bars`, same name in Rust and Python).

StrategyManifest.description: A verified, hashable description of a strategy, ready to be run.

api_version.description: Strategy contract version this was compiled against.

driving_timeframe.description: The bar timeframe that drives the strategy's clock.

name.description: Strategy's declared name, used in journals and reports.

parameters.description: Optional parameter declarations defining defaults and search spaces (E4-S2).

schedules.description: Optional wall-clock schedules (session open/close, rebalance times).

source_hash.description:
Stable digest of the source that produced this manifest.

Two runs with the same `source_hash` and the same data must produce a byte-identical journal; a changed hash is what tells a cache it cannot reuse a previous result.

subscriptions.description: What the strategy needs fed to it.

universe.description: The universe the strategy may trade, as a named set or explicit list.

warmup_bars.description: Bars required before the first decision, so indicators converge.

StreamFrame.description:
One frame of the run event stream (ADR 0021, `GET /backtests/{id}/events`).

A `Record` frame carries one journal `Message` with its 0-based line index; a `Status` frame carries the manifest status with `seq` = the number of journal records delivered so far. Every frame's `seq` is a valid resume token: resuming at `N` replays records with line index `>= N`, so the stream neither skips nor repeats a record across a reconnect.

oneOf.description: The run's lifecycle state; emitted on connect, on every status change, and once more (terminal) when the stream ends. `error` is present only for a failed run.

error.description: Why the run failed; present only when `status` is `failed`.

seq.description: Next journal line index to read (records delivered so far).
The record's 0-based line index in `events.ndjson` industries.

Subscriptions.description:
The market data a strategy subscribes to.

A strategy that forgets a subscription gets no events for it, which in a backtest looks like a strategy that never trades. Recording the set explicitly is what lets the loader fail loudly instead.

instruments.description: Instruments whose bars this strategy consumes.

SweepReportResponse.description: Sweep results: best trials plus the ranking, in a deterministic order.

ranked.description: Trials ranked best-first by the fitness function.

validation.description: Statistical overfitting validation block across sweep trials (E4-S6).

SweepRequest.description:
Sweep request.

Every field is optional on the wire, but `SweepRequest::resolve` requires `seed` (non-zero), `strategy`, `params` and `trials` (ADR 0017 decision 6).

params.description: Parameter ranges, as a JSON object of name to [low, high, step].

seed.description: Seed; required and non-zero on submit.

error.description: Why the job failed; present only when `status` is `failed`.

TimeInForce.description: How long an order remains active.

oneOf.description: Valid until the end of the trading day.

Timeframe.description: Bar or indicator timeframe dimension for technical metrics.

interval.description: Number of units per bar, e.g. 5 in `5m`.

Trade.description:
A completed fill, recorded after the exchange confirms execution.

`costs` is the total transaction cost of the fill (brokerage, taxes, exchange fees) as [`Money`] in the settlement currency; it defaults to zero and is set with [`Trade::with_costs`]. `quantity` and `price` stay `f64`: they are observations, and [`Trade::notional`] rounds to minor units once, at the point of use.

``` use honba_entities::{Currency, Trade}; use honba_messages::{InstrumentId, OrderId, OrderSide, UnixNanos, Exchange};

let t = Trade::new( OrderId::new("O-1"), InstrumentId::new("NIFTY50", Exchange::new("NSE")), OrderSide::Buy, 75.0, 22_000.0, Currency::Inr, UnixNanos::from_u64(1), UnixNanos::from_u64(2), ); assert_eq!(t.notional(), 75.0 * 22_000.0); assert_eq!(t.costs().minor(), 0); ```

Invariants (checked by [`Trade::validate`] and on deserialization): `side` is buy or sell, `quantity` and `price` are finite and `> 0`. Costs are an integer `Money` and so cannot be non-finite.

TradingState.description:
Whether the engine is trading, winding down, or stopped.

A handler asks for a change with `EngineOutput::StateChange` (in `honba-engine`); the engine applies it through [`TradingState::can_transition_to`] and records it in its audit log.

oneOf.description: Winding down: orders are still accepted, the strategy is reducing.
Stopped: orders are refused until the state changes again.

TradingStateChange.description:
`PUT /trading-state` response: the state now in force and the one it replaced.

`previous == state` means the request changed nothing.

previous.description: The trading state before this request.

state.description: The trading state now in force.

TradingStateRequest.description:
`PUT /trading-state` request body: the state the operator wants (ADR 0018 decision 7).

Every transition is allowed and setting the current state again is a no-op. `reason` is free text for the operator log.

reason.description: Why the state is changing; logged with the change, never interpreted.

TradingStateResponse.description: `GET /trading-state` response: the operator trading state the write routes evaluate against.

UnitType.description: Unit of measurement for a metric.

Universe.description: The set of instruments a strategy may trade.

oneOf.description: A named index or curated list resolved by the broker adapter.

UnixNanos.description: JSON representation of UnixNanos with ISO-8601 string and unix_nanos string.

ValidationBlock.description: Comprehensive statistical validation block for a backtest or parameter sweep.

monte_carlo.description: Block-bootstrap Monte Carlo drawdown and ruin simulation result.

passed.description: Overall verdict: true only if all evaluated gates passed.

pbo.description: Probability of Backtest Overfitting validation result (for multi-trial sweeps).

oneOf.description: Floating point or integer numeric value.

VenueOrderId.description: A venue-assigned order identifier (the exchange or broker's id, as opposed to the client-assigned [`OrderId`]).

passed.description: Whether the strategy passes walk-forward stability requirements.
